absent: Absolute on-disk corpus paths for routed files: AUSENTE from lane data.
Numeric sizes for blocks, sections, subsections, pageblocks and direct-map ceiling: AUSENTE.
Full layouts of page descriptors, memory sections, node data, alternate maps and device maps beyond touched fields: AUSENTE.
Synchronization for sparse and vmemmap population beyond hotplug bracketing and callback mutex: AUSENTE.
Demotion, reclaim, slab and migration policies beyond the toggle edge and allocation-failure reporting: AUSENTE.
Architecture-specific range hook behavior, early-section detection and subsection-map encoding: AUSENTE.
Offline and removal paths and recovery after partial multi-section failure: AUSENTE.

findings.text: A NUMA memory-tier control exposes a readable and writable boolean toggle through the memory sysfs hierarchy. Reading renders the current enablement as text; writing parses a new boolean value.

During early initialization a dedicated NUMA grouping object is created beneath the memory object and a single-entry attribute collection is attached to it. Failure to attach discards the created object and propagates the error.

Updating the demotion toggle only acts on a disabled-to-enabled transition, where it iterates all online nodes to reset hopeless reclaim counters. Unparseable input fails without changing state; other writes simply store the value.

Descriptor-on-added-memory placement has disable, enable and forced states with disable as the initial setting. One build reports active whenever not disabled, while an alternate build always reports inactive.

Storage needed for descriptors of one hotplug block grows with the number of frames the block covers multiplied by descriptor size. Required pages round up, with additional pageblock rounding applied solely in forced mode.

The placement-mode control accepts two capitalizations of the forced keyword and otherwise interprets input as a boolean to select enable or disable. Selecting forced emits a one-time notice about per-block waste caused by alignment. Reading renders forced distinctly from the boolean states.
Zone-selection policy for onlining starts in contiguous-zone mode with an automatic movable alternative. Associated tunables start at a fixed ratio and with NUMA awareness enabled.
Policy updates resolve the supplied name through a string table and reject unknown names without changing state. Retrieval formats the active entry back to its name.
A dedicated mutex guards replacement of the routine used to online a page. The initial routine is a generic implementation.

Movable-node handling starts disabled. The default type for newly added memory starts unset and is resolved lazily on first query from build configuration, defaulting to offline when no configuration selects otherwise.
An early boot option translates a textual state name into the default online type. Unrecognized names leave the stored default unchanged.
Entering a hotplug operation acquires CPU read protection and then write ownership of the hotplug control; leaving releases in reverse order.
A global ceiling for boot-time memory discovery starts at the maximum unsigned value. Additions that exceed it are rejected only while the system has not yet reached running state.

Registering a new range first checks pluggability and the boot ceiling, then requests ownership from the global memory resource pool. Ranges whose name differs from the conventional system memory label are flagged as driver managed. Oversize and collision cases fail with distinct errors and emit diagnostics.
Releasing a registered range is a no-op for a null handle. Otherwise it relinquishes the reservation and frees the descriptor.

A candidate range is allowed only when it is non-empty and fully enclosed by the pluggable interval; violations warn. The pluggable interval derives from an architecture hook clipped to the direct-map maximum when a mapping is required, otherwise it spans from zero to that maximum. The default hook covers the whole address space.
Sparse addition requires the start frame and length, when combined, to honor subsection granularity. Violations fail validation.

Adding pages validates protection state, addressability, alternate-map containment and alignment before looping over section-bounded extents with scheduling opportunities between extents. Alternate-map requests must start at the same frame and fit within the request, with the allocation cursor reset on entry. The first extent failure determines the result.

Adding a section prepares its index, activates backing storage, scrubs fresh descriptors to catch invalid flag combinations, marks the section present, adjusts the base for subsection starts, and initializes per-section metadata.

Activation creates the usage record on first touch and records subsection coverage, freeing the record if coverage fails. Partial additions into early sections reuse existing storage; full additions populate new storage and roll back coverage when population fails.
After each section-map attempt the system accounts for the descriptor pages attributable to the frame interval, taking alternate mapping aids into account.

Low-level population requires subsection alignment and then selects between an optimized compound path and a generic path based on eligibility. Success flushes the relevant cache range and returns the descriptor base; failure returns null.

Optimized population either reuses tail storage established by an earlier iteration or processes the interval in bounded pieces, establishing distinct head and representative tail entries per piece and sharing one frame with held references for the remaining tails.

Populating a virtual address ensures each translation level exists from the top down to the leaf, failing if any level cannot be created, and then performs a locality verification over the new mapping.

Leaf creation preserves already-present entries. New leaves either obtain a fresh frame or reuse a caller-supplied frame, holding an extra reference in the shared-tail case, and install the entry with kernel mapping attributes in the initial address space.
Mapping verification compares the node of the backing frame against the requested node and warns once when the distance exceeds the local threshold.

Backing storage for translation tables prefers caller-provided alternate space when present. Otherwise it uses the page allocator once slab is ready with a retryable quiet request and a single warning on failure, falling back to constrained early reservation when slab is unavailable.

Allocation-failure reporting is rate limited and skipped for quiet requests or for DMA requests on systems without managed DMA. When emitted it reports the caller, mode and node mask, current allowance, stack trace and a memory summary whose node filtering is relaxed for out-of-memory victims, privileged allocation contexts, non-task contexts and non-reclaiming requests.
Early descriptor reservation uses raw block allocation with leak tracing disabled, either pinned to an exact node or best-effort, and scrubs the reservation when the length is positive.

Alternate-space allocation rejects non-page multiples, derives alignment from the request size, fails when free space is insufficient, and otherwise advances allocation and alignment counters and returns the virtual address of the chosen frames. The next free position combines base, reservation and both counters; remaining free space never goes negative.

A NUMA attribute collection is a null-terminated pointer list containing one read-write toggle, attached through a group descriptor. Two parameter-operation records each bind a custom string parser with a matching renderer for placement mode and for online policy.
Creating a missing intermediate table allocates a zeroed page, initializes it as a table page, and links it into its parent.
Placement codes are disable zero, enable one and forced two. Online-policy codes are contiguous zones zero and automatic movable one.
User-visible names are group numa and toggle demotion_enabled; forced accepts force and FORCE and renders as force; boolean states render as Y and N; policies are contig-zones and auto-movable.

Public helpers in scope query allowed and pluggable ranges, manage default online types, bracket hotplug operations, add page ranges and sparse sections, populate and verify descriptor maps, allocate backing blocks, report allocation failures and reserve early descriptor storage.

Invalid hot-add parameters, including missing protection, out-of-range addresses, mismatched alternate maps and misaligned extents, are rejected with warnings and no partial effect. Oversize reservations and collisions likewise fail cleanly.

Initial tunables are placement disabled, online policy contiguous, movable ratio 301, NUMA awareness true, movable nodes false, default online type -1 meaning unresolved, and boot ceiling at maximum unsigned value.
